default_configuration.description: The build configuration to fall back on when neither `--configuration` nor a persisted selection names one: a tag declared on rules; a name no rule declares is an error. Unset, the first declared tag is used.

cache_dir.description: Directory for the unified on-disk cache (PCHs, PCMs and the index), relative to the project root. Empty defaults to `${workspace}/.clice`, which keeps itself out of version control and backups via generated .gitignore and CACHEDIR.TAG markers (a `.clice/config.toml` stays visible to Git; backup tools honoring CACHEDIR.TAG skip the whole directory); an explicitly configured directory is never marked. It must be a directory clice can write on a local disk: a project whose cache directory cannot be written or is on a network file system (NFS, SMB, a Windows drive under WSL) serves nothing, and clice says why. Files outside every workspace folder keep theirs in clice's temporary directory, removed when the server exits. The resolved path is printed at startup.

logging_dir.description: Directory for log files, relative to the project root; empty derives `${cache_dir}/logs`. Each server, `clice index` and `clice lint` run logs into a subdirectory of its own; the 20 latest are kept.

poll_seconds.description: Longest interval in seconds between two background looks at a project file: the interval doubles at every look that finds the file unchanged, up to this. 0 disables background polling, compilation databases included.

documentation.description: The [documentation] section: how documentation comments are read.

document_symbols.description: The [document_symbols] section: what the outline lists.

semantic_tokens.description: The [semantic_tokens] section: what the semantic tokens hold and the names they are sent by.

references.description: The [references] section: what find references answers.

rules.description: File-pattern rules: where files take their commands from and how they are compiled, served, indexed, linted and formatted ([[rules]] in clice.toml). Rules given through initializationOptions replace the file's.

foreground.description: Number of foreground workers: they keep the open files compiled and answer the requests about them (hover, semantic tokens, ...); at least 1.

background.description: The most compiles the background index runs at once, never more than `max`: "auto", half the machine's physical cores and at least 2, or a number, at least 1. Raising it speeds a first index up on a big machine.

max.description: The most compile workers at once, the background index's, completion's, signature help's and the precompiled headers' and modules' together: "auto", the machine's physical cores, or a number, at least 1. They start as work needs them and stop after 30 seconds idle.

background_delay_ms.description: How long the background index waits after the last edit or request before it starts, in milliseconds.

clang_tidy.description: Run clang-tidy on open files and offer its fixes, with the checks the nearest `.clang-tidy` configures (a small default set without one). Checks too slow for an editor are left out unless `slow_clang_tidy_checks` is `true`, those unreliable on code being edited always are; files `clice lint` does not check get none. `NOLINT` comments also silence compiler warnings only while this runs.

slow_clang_tidy_checks.description: Also run on open files the checks the `.clang-tidy` enables that are too slow for an editor or not measured for one (`misc-const-correctness` doubles the time a large file takes to compile): every compile of the file waits for them. Unset, clice names such checks once when it leaves them out; `false` leaves them out silently. `clice lint` runs them either way.

suppress.description: Diagnostics open files do not show, by their code: a compiler warning's option (`-Wunused-variable`), clang's name for any other diagnostic (`err_undeclared_var_use`), a clang-tidy check, or one of clice's own warnings (`toolchain-query-failed`). For code clang gets wrong: everything else works on the file as before, and `clice lint` still reports them.

format.description: How documentation comments are read, wherever they show (hover, completion, signature help, `clice query`): "doxygen" reads Doxygen's commands (`@brief`, `@param`, `@return`, ...) and the Markdown Doxygen allows, along with the GTK-Doc and kernel-doc conventions; "plain" shows a comment as written.

inherit.description: An overriding method without a documentation comment shows the one of the method it overrides.

show_aka.description: Show what a type alias stands for, e.g. `size_type` is `unsigned long`.

max_members.description: Maximum number of members the definition of a hovered class or enum lists: data members and member types, or enumerators; member functions are left out. `0` shows the declaration alone.

layout.description: Show how the compiler lays out a class or a field wherever it is hovered: size, alignment, a field's offset, and the padding.

macros.description: List the `#define`s the file writes; an include guard's never lists.

locals.description: List what a function's body declares: its variables, types and lambdas, under the function.

types.description: Maximum length in characters of a deduced type or of deduced template arguments, or `"unlimited"`. The template arguments that do not fit become `…`, e.g. `tuple<int, string, …>`; a type whose outermost name does not fit is not shown.

default_arguments.description: Maximum length in characters of the omitted default arguments, or `"unlimited"`. One too long becomes `…`, and the list is cut with `…` where it no longer fits.

block_end.description: Maximum length in characters of a block end or namespace end label, cut with `…` past it, or `"unlimited"`.

endif.description: Maximum length in characters of an `#endif` condition, cut with `…` past it, or `"unlimited"`.

enabled.description: Master switch: `false` disables all inlay hints.

parameters.description: Parameter name hints at call sites, e.g. `draw(width: 800, height: 600)`.

mutable_references.description: `&` marking an argument passed by mutable reference, e.g. `mutate(&value: v)`.

prefixed_names.description: Parameter name hints for an argument named like the parameter without its one-letter prefix, e.g. `param` passed to `aParam`.

single_letter_names.description: Parameter name hints for a function taking one parameter whose name is a single letter, e.g. `push_back(x: 1)`.

deduced_types.description: Deduced type hints for `auto` variables, structured bindings, init-captures and `auto` parameters, the type a `decltype` names, and deduced return types.

spelled_types.description: Deduced type hints for a variable whose initializer already names its type, e.g. `static_cast<long>(x)`, `Widget{1, 2}` or `std::make_unique<Widget>()`.

deduced_template_arguments.description: The template arguments class template argument deduction found, e.g. `<int, double>` after `pair` in `std::pair pair(1, 2.5)`.

designators.description: Field designator hints in aggregate initialization, e.g. `.x=` and `.y=` in `Point{1, 2}`.

array_indices.description: Array index designator hints in aggregate initialization, e.g. `[0]=` and `[1]=` in `int pair[2] = {1, 2}`.

block_end.description: `// name` after the closing brace of a function, type or control flow block, linking to its start.

namespace_end.description: `// namespace name` after the closing brace of a namespace, linking to its start.

endif.description: `// condition` after an `#endif`, the condition of the `#if` it closes, linking to it.

default_arguments.description: The default arguments a call omitted.

min_block_lines.description: The height in lines, both ends included, from which a block, namespace or conditional gets a hint at its end.

max_length.description: The [inlay_hints.max_length] table: how long each kind of hint may grow.

lexical.description: Send the tokens an editor's own syntax highlighting colors as well: keywords, literals, comments, operators, preprocessor directives. When off, only what syntax cannot tell is sent: names by what they name, overloaded and declarator operators, template brackets, format specifiers, and the tokens of preprocessor-inactive code, kindless.

kinds.description: The names a client or theme expects for clice's token kinds, as `field = "property"`; an empty name drops the kind, whose tokens are then not sent, and kinds given one name merge. Read when the server starts.

modifiers.description: The names a client or theme expects for clice's token modifiers; an empty name drops the modifier, and modifiers given one name merge. Read when the server starts.

arguments.description: What completing a call or a template inserts after the name: "placeholders" its parentheses or angle brackets with a placeholder per parameter, "delimiters" the empty parentheses or brackets with the cursor between them, "none" the name alone. It applies to functions, function-like macros, variables holding a lambda and class, alias and variable templates; an overload set listed as one item takes the delimiters. Nothing is added where the arguments are written already or the name is not called, as when taking a function's address. Clients without snippet support get the parentheses of a call alone. An Objective-C message takes a placeholder or an empty tab stop after each piece of its selector, its first piece alone with "none" or without snippet support.

bundle_overloads.description: Collapse an overload set into a single completion item.

statement_snippets.description: Complete statements such as `if` and `for` as snippets with placeholders for their parts; otherwise only the keyword is inserted. Ignored for clients without snippet support.

dot_to_arrow.description: After `.` on a pointer, list the members `->` reaches and turn the `.` into `->` when one is chosen.

all_scopes.description: Where an unqualified name is being typed, also offer the project's names of other namespaces it matches, inserting the qualifier they need; one in several namespaces is offered once per namespace. Names the file reaches already are offered as they are; for the others see `insert_includes` and `insert_imports`. The names of other namespaces come from the index.

insert_includes.description: With `all_scopes`, also offer names declared, and macros defined, in headers the file does not include yet, adding the `#include` of the header that holds them.

angled_includes.description: Glob patterns of the headers whose `#include`, added by completion or a code action, takes angle brackets, matched against the path written between them (`fmt/core.h`) with the syntax of a rule's `patterns`: `fmt/**` matches every header below `fmt/`. A header neither this nor `quoted_includes` matches takes quotes when found next to the file or through `-iquote` or `-I`, and angle brackets when found through `-isystem`, `-idirafter` or a framework directory; one an IWYU pragma names to include instead keeps the pragma's. A header found through the toolchain's own directories, the standard library's, always takes angle brackets. A pattern is followed even where its delimiters do not find the header: angle brackets do not search the file's own directory or `-iquote`.

quoted_includes.description: Glob patterns of the headers whose `#include`, added by completion or a code action, takes quotes, as `angled_includes` describes. A header both match takes quotes: `angled_includes = ["**"]` with `quoted_includes = ["myproj/**"]` gives every header angle brackets but the project's own.

insert_imports.description: With `all_scopes`, also offer names exported by modules the file does not import yet, adding the `import`. Where the project builds the `std` module, a file that imports modules or is a module unit takes the standard library's names with `import std;` rather than their headers.

limit.description: Maximum number of completion items, the best ranked, or `"unlimited"`. A list cut short is marked incomplete, so the editor asks again as you type.

documentation.description: Show the called function's documentation comment.

limit.description: Maximum number of locations a references request answers with, or `"unlimited"`. A reply cut short keeps the locations in the file it is asked from before any other. `clice query references` lists every one.

patterns.description: Glob patterns selecting the files this rule applies to. A relative pattern is anchored at the project root (`..` segments allowed); an absolute pattern or one starting with `**` matches the file's absolute path: its real path, symlinks resolved, or the path the build reaches it by, either one (Bazel's `external/...`, linked from elsewhere). `*` matches within a path segment, `?` a single character, `**` any number of segments, `{a,b}` alternatives, `[0-9]` a character range, `[!...]` a negated range, `[*]` a literal `*`. Separators are `/` on every platform. Omitted means every file: such a rule belongs last, where it decides what no rule above it does.

configuration.description: Build configuration tag. A tagged rule applies only while that configuration is active; an untagged rule always applies. The distinct tags form the configuration menu; `--configuration`, the persisted selection and `default_configuration` pick the active one, in that order.

compile_commands.description: Compilation databases, in priority order: a compile_commands.json or a directory containing one, relative to the project root. All of them load, and every entry applies to its own file whatever the patterns say; the patterns and the order decide which entry a file present in several databases gets by default. A rule without patterns names the project's databases. When no rule declares a source, every compile_commands.json in the project root and its immediate subdirectories loads, and so do the ones in the directories above a file when it is opened; a directory below the root with a clice.toml or .clice/config.toml of its own is another project, and none in it loads.

resolve_symlinks.description: Whether builds are told apart by the real paths this rule's `compile_commands` resolve to, through symlinks and Windows junctions, rather than by the configuration's name: for a build system that selects a build by pointing a link at its directory. Each real path keeps an index of its own, and when the link is pointed elsewhere the server asks to be restarted on that build's index, which still holds what an earlier session indexed there. A configuration whose rules differ from this configuration's only in naming exactly those databases directly shares its index. The index of a build no longer used stays in the cache directory until deleted.

default_command.description: The compile command for matching files without a database entry, without the source file: a string tokenized like a shell command line, or an argv array. It runs from the project root, and the matching source files on disk join the background index (unless `background_index` is `false`) — enumerated at startup and again on every poll, so a file created later compiles when opened and joins the index within a poll period. A file clang has no language for (an Arduino `.ino`, an extensionless tool) is a source only when the command forces a language (`-x c++`) and a pattern names its suffix (`*.ino`) or the file itself. Omitted means none.

append.description: Compilation flags appended for matching files, e.g. `["-std=c++20", "-DNDEBUG"]`. The flags of every matching rule apply, in declaration order.

remove.description: Compilation flags removed for matching files, e.g. `["-Wall"]`, before the rule's own `append`. A flag with a value removes that value (`-DDEBUG`), the next element being a separate value as on a command line; one with `*` for its value (`-I*`, `["-include", "*"]`), or without one at the end of the list (`["-include"]`), removes every value; a `*` right after a flag's name removes every flag of its kind spelled with that prefix (`-W*` takes `-Wall` and `-Wextra` too).

query_toolchain.description: Whether clice runs the compiler of matching files' commands to ask how it compiles them: its target, standard library and system headers, predefined macros and default language standard. `false` runs no compiler: clice's own clang reads the command as written, with clang's defaults for the compiler's name. Unset means `true`.

background_index.description: Whether the background index compiles matching files as translation units of their own. `false` keeps them out, and drops what an earlier index recorded of them: they still compile when opened, and a header among them is still indexed through the units including it. A module unit, or the unit writing a precompiled header, is indexed all the same by the build of its module or header, for the files reading it. A rule without patterns saying `false` keeps the background index from compiling anything. Unset means `true`.

skip_function_body.description: Whether the compiles that include matching files skip their function bodies. Unset, the editor's compile of an open file skips the bodies of the headers it includes at its top — several times faster to open and rebuild, the errors inside those bodies shown once the background index has compiled the file as saved — and every other compile reads them. `true`: every compile but a matching file's own skips its bodies, templates' included, the background index's too, and none of them is indexed — the fastest index of code you only call, such as third-party libraries, whose templates' errors your code causes are then never shown. The bodies of templates forwarding their arguments (`make_unique`) and of `constexpr` and `auto` functions are read all the same. `false`: no compile skips them, and their errors show at once.

index_function_body.description: Whether the index records what the function bodies of matching files use, and what their templates' instantiations resolve, so that references and the call hierarchy reach inside them. Unset means `false` for system headers — a library's own internals, which only a reader of its code asks about — and `true` for every other file. A file opened in the editor is indexed whole all the same. Applies to the units indexed after a change.

readonly.description: How matching files are served when open: "off" compiles them — builds are pulled by the first request that needs them, with the index answering in the meantime; "on" builds no preamble PCH — reads serve from the index alone (a cold file jumps the indexing queue), while completion and signature help still compile on demand without a preamble; "auto" starts a file as "on", switches it to "off" at the first edit intent (edit, completion, signature help, context switch), and falls back to "off" for a file the index cannot serve. Unset means "off".

self_contained.description: Whether matching headers compile on their own. `true`: a header compiles alone, without an includer's context; `false`: always in the context of a file including it. Unset, clice compiles a header alone once to find out.

other_contexts.description: Whether an open matching file shows, in the code its own context skips, what its other contexts compile there — the semantic colors, outline, folds, links and hover the index holds for them — while it is as the index read it. `false` shows its own context alone. The editor's choice for a file (Show or Hide other contexts) overrides it until the server stops. Unset means `true`.

lint.description: Whether `clice lint` checks matching files and the editor runs clang-tidy on them. `false` keeps them out: their findings are dropped and a translation unit they head is not parsed, unless `--index` needs it for the index. Files outside the project are never checked. Unset means `true`.

format.description: Whether `clice format` formats matching files. `false` keeps them out. Files outside the project are never formatted. Unset means `true`.
